passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of three different auditory cues on the speed of visual search tasks. Participants were randomly assigned to one of four conditions: (1) no cue, (2) a low‑frequency tone, (3) a high‑frequency tone, and (4) a rhythmic beat. Each participant performed 50 trials, and the mean response time (RT) and standard deviation (SD) were recorded. The data suggest that rhythmic beats may facilitate faster visual search, but the effect size varies across individuals. The study also examined whether the participants’ prior musical training moderated the cue effect. The authors concluded that while rhythmic cues generally improve performance, the benefit is most pronounced in musically trained participants. Future research should investigate whether similar effects occur with other sensory modalities and whether training can enhance the cueing advantage.
stem: Which condition yielded the lowest mean response time?
explanation: The table shows the mean RT for each condition; the rhythmic beat condition has the smallest mean (720 ms).
trap: The low‑frequency tone condition (780 ms) is close to the rhythmic beat and could be mistakenly chosen.

stem: Which variable is the independent variable in this experiment?
explanation: The independent variable is the factor that the researchers manipulate; here it is the type of auditory cue presented to participants.
trap: Participants’ musical training (D) is a moderator, not the primary manipulated variable.

stem: Calculate the coefficient of variation (CV) for the rhythmic beat condition.
explanation: CV = SD / mean = 105 / 720 ≈ 0.146, which rounds to 0.15 (option B).
trap: Dividing the rhythmic-beat SD (105 ms) by the no-cue mean (850 ms), which gives about 0.12, instead of by the rhythmic-beat mean (720 ms).

stem: Which of the following is NOT a valid conclusion based on the data in the table?

options.A: Mean response time was lower with rhythmic beats than with no cue.
options.B: Mean response time was lower with high-frequency tones than with no cue.
options.C: Low-frequency tones produce the fastest mean response time.
options.D: The SD of response time was smaller in the rhythmic beat condition than in the no-cue condition.

explanation: Correct: C) The rhythmic beat condition has the fastest mean RT (720 ms), faster than low-frequency tones (780 ms). Why the others are wrong: A) 720 ms is lower than 850 ms. B) 800 ms is lower than 850 ms. D) SD was 105 ms vs 120 ms.
trap: Picking the low-frequency tone because its mean (780 ms) is the second-lowest and close to the rhythmic value.

stem: By what percent was the mean response time in the rhythmic beat condition lower than in the no-cue condition?
explanation: Correct: (850 - 720) / 850 x 100 = 15.3%. Why the others are wrong: B) 8.2% is the reduction for the low-frequency tone ((850 - 780)/850). C) 18.1% divides by the rhythmic mean (130/720) instead of the no-cue mean. D) 5.9% is the reduction for the high-frequency tone.
trap: Dividing the difference by the rhythmic mean instead of the no-cue reference.
